correctness.rationale: The graphical-group commutator is M_x, so its conjugation classes above x are cosets of image M_x. Unit scaling yields a representative with each vertex coordinate pi^a. A square minor of M_a is the corresponding totally unimodular incidence minor multiplied by one monomial; nonzero minors are precisely rooted forests and have the explicit valuation c_F(a). Smith normal form over the DVR yields integer exponents d_i from consecutive determinantal minima, and reduction modulo pi^ell gives the image size q^s. Each nonzero valuation shell has (q-1)q^(ell-a-1) choices. Summing produces exact class-size polynomials with nonnegative q-1 coefficients. Independent enumerations and integer-minor checks passed 44 test assertions, including noncograph graphs and residue characteristic two; examples are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Rossmann–Voll (2019), Theorem E establishes levelwise nonnegative q-1 class-number coefficients for cographs, not arbitrary graphs, and Question 1.7 asks which other graphs enjoy it. Rossmann (2021 preprint; 2022 publication), Corollary C proves all-graph class-size positivity only for the first congruence level, and Section 8 describes unresolved higher levels. The new forest-minor Smith-invariant formula proves a strictly stronger statement at every finite congruence level and for each conjugacy-class size. Relevant public research-record searches located graphical-group character-degree distributions and cograph/finite-field work, not an implication of this theorem. Full-text assessments are recorded separately; possible broad valuation-minor literature remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The result answers Rossmann–Voll 2019 Question 1.7 by establishing all-level q-1 positivity for arbitrary graphs, beyond the previously proven cograph theorem, and strengthens the answer by conjugacy-class-size strata. The formula uses concrete spanning-forest valuations for all graph shapes including cycles, making a natural finite invariant structurally computable; no general analytic-pole or rational closed form is asserted.
